archetype: Sustained-DPM bossing class; damage comes from consistent output across the whole fight rather than from a single large burst window.

Grandis Library's own skill data (re-read 2026-09-12) actually says +130 all stat, agreeing with maplestorywiki rather than with the class doc - see conflicts.

There is no redundancy problem: Grandis's own note explains that a trio is built from each node's MAIN skill (the skill at the top) and that 'Nodes with the same Main Skill (skill at the top) cannot be equipped at the same time', so three different main skills drawn from one enhancement group is legal.

trios.sourceCountNote: Same two lineages as the bossing trio.

vMatrix.notes: Fifth job and the V Matrix open at Lv. 200. The class doc is explicit that its node order is a preference, not a fixed rule, and that you should unlock most or all nodes before maxing any of them. Grandis states that 4 boost nodes in total are needed to reach Master Level 60 for these skills (with Matrix Points used), and that nodes sharing a main skill cannot be equipped together. Nautilus Strike is the class's counter-intuitive pick: it is boosted despite never being cast, purely for the two final-attack hits its passive grants to other skills.

order.step: Unlock some HEXA Mastery nodes first, then unlock Sol Janus.
order.why: Verbatim in the class doc: 'You should unlock Sol Janus right after you unlocked some of the masteries as this skill helps a lot with both farming and just doing dailies/weeklies. Our mobbing capabilities were considered below average, but Sol Janus equalised all of the classes.'

order.step: Level Sol Janus to a breakpoint that matches how much you actually farm: stay at 1 if you only do dailies and weeklies; go to 10 if you farm at least 30 minutes; go to 20 if you farm with WAPs; go to 30 only if you are farming heavily or pushing to Lv. 290 or higher.
order.why: The class doc gives this exact four-tier guideline. Its supporting claim - 'Sol Janus has major upgrades at levels 10, 20 and 30. The levels in-between only increases the damage dealt and XP gained' - is corroborated by maplestorywiki's Sol Janus level table, where the passive EXP bonus steps from 26% at Lv. 9 to 37% at Lv. 10, from 55% at Lv. 19 to 67% at Lv. 20, and from 85% at Lv. 29 to 100% at Lv. 30.
order.sourceCountNote: The farming-tier guideline itself is class doc only; maplestorywiki independently confirms only the 10/20/30 breakpoint structure it rests on.

order.step: Start HEXA Stat only after several skills are at level 10.
order.why: Verbatim in the class doc: 'It is recommended to start this after you have leveled some of your skills to Level 10. On average, the cost for maxing your HEXA stat is approximately 300 fragments.'

order.step: For HEXA Stat, choose three main stats from Attack, Strength, Boss and Critical Damage; level to 20 and sit there for now.
order.why: The class doc names exactly those four candidates and says 'For the time being, it is recommended just to level it to 20 and sit on it for now. The higher your main stat the better, but it is very min-max to reset at the moment.' It adds that duplicate main stats are not allowed across cores, so rotate the chosen stats between HEXA Stat I, II and III or use a calculator.

hexa.orderNote: These four steps are sequenced as the class doc sequences them, and step 1's position is stated outright by the doc ('right after you unlocked some of the masteries'), not inferred from page layout. They cover Sol Janus and HEXA Stat sequencing ONLY - they are not a per-node levelling order. See knownGap.

knownGap.field: per-node HEXA levelling priority (which mastery/enhancement to raise in which order)
knownGap.detail: The Buccaneer Bible does carry a HEXA node priority chart, headed 'HEXA Matrix Priority [Updated 9/10/2026]' and described in the body as updated for the Frieren Collab Patch and including the new Common node - but the chart itself is an embedded image. Re-read as raw text 2026-09-12: the surrounding prose extracts, the chart does not. It has deliberately NOT been guessed at. An earlier automated extraction produced a plausible-looking numbered HEXA order that does not exist in the document; it was discarded as a fabrication. Grandis Library has no HEXA section for any class. Fill this only by reading the chart image by eye or asking in the Buccaneer Discord.

masteryNodes: Mastery Node/Core 2: HEXA Sea Serpent, HEXA Nautilus Strike
verifiedNodeNames.sourceCountNote: Verbatim in-game skill data from maplestorywiki, but only one page reached carries a HEXA node table for this class, so it is labelled weak on the source-count rule.

hexa.notes: Sixth job opens at Lv. 260 (maplestorywiki gives Level Requirement 260 on every HEXA Enhancement). maplestorywiki also states that Final Damage bonuses from HEXA Enhancements increase linearly per level with a jump at levels 10, 20 and 30, and that Enhancements require the corresponding V skill to be maxed and equipped.

priority.why: The class doc writes this as an explicit arrow-ordered priority: 'Boss Damage % -> Damage % -> Critical Damage % -> IED % -> Attack -> STR'. Its stated allocation rule is to distribute the majority of points 'evenly' across the first four and spend leftover points on the remaining two. Critical Rate is deliberately absent because, in the doc's words, 'Buccaneer already has over 100% critical rate when attacking bosses'.

Also written as an explicit arrow-ordered priority in the class doc: 'EXP % -> Critical Rate -> Mob Damage % -> Damage % -> Critical Damage % -> Attack -> STR', prefaced by 'we of course want to maximize our EXP as soon as possible' and followed by 'It is recommended to use Legion and Hyper Stat together to boost critical rate for mobbing.'

hyperStats.orderNote: Both arrays are ordered on purpose and the source states the order literally, with arrows - array position here is warranted, not invented. It is a priority of allocation, not a fixed point spread: the doc says outright 'there is no standardized hyper stat build' and 'Optimizing your hyper stats takes into account numerous factors and can vary greatly on your level of progression', and points readers at SuckHard's hyper stat calculator for a per-character answer.

examples.bossing: Class doc worked example for Lv. 280 at 300% DEF: STR 3, Critical Damage 13, Ignore Enemy DEF 10, Damage 13, Boss Damage 14, Attack 7.
examples.training: Class doc worked example for Lv. 280: Critical Rate 6, Critical Damage 11, Damage 12, Monster Damage 12, Attack 5, EXP 15.

hyperStats.notes: Hyper stat points begin at Lv. 140, so this is the first of these systems a Lv. 140 Buccaneer can act on.

hyperSkills.passivesOrderNote: Stored unordered. Neither source ranks the five picks against each other; you take all five in a build, so array position carries no priority.
hyperSkills.passiveEffects: Class doc values, re-read 2026-09-12: Double Down - Saving Grace = 40% chance to ignore cooldown when Double Down does not activate (the next cast then activates Double Down with a 4 or above); Double Down - Enhance = increased chance of rolling 4, 5 or 6; Reinforce = +20% damage; Boss Rush = +20% boss damage; Spread = +2 max enemies hit; Extra Strike = +1 number of attacks.
actives: Serpent Spirit - became a passive skill as of the One Punch Man collaboration update; gives a passive 15% Critical Damage
Epic Adventure - damage buff that also buffs other Explorers in the party, 120 second cooldown
Stimulating Conversation - damage buff; the Sea Serpent skills get -50% cooldown and Lord of the Deep gets -50% cooldown, 120 second cooldown
hyperSkills.sourceCountNote: Grandis Library gives passive lists identical to the class doc's, but its Credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc' - one lineage, not two votes. Downgraded from 'moderate' on 2026-09-12 for that reason. The actives are class doc only either way.
hyperSkills.notes: The bossing and mobbing passive sets differ only in whether the three offensive picks go on Octopunch or Hook Bomber; both keep the two Double Down lines.

ideal: +8% damage when attacking targets inflicted with Abnormal Status
innerAbility.idealOrderNote: Stored unordered. The class doc's prose names them as a set - 'Buccaneer's ideal inner ability is Boss Damage, Buff Duration and Abnormal Status' - while its bullet list runs Boss Damage, Abnormal Status, Buff Duration, a different order again. Neither source ranks the three lines, so array position must not be read as priority. The earlier '(top line)' annotation on Boss Damage was DELETED on 2026-09-12: no source reached states which inner ability slot it must occupy.
alternatives: Meso Obtained (Unique or Legendary) - the doc's pick for Reboot players: 'Temporarily trading damage to earn more meso is beneficial to progression.'
Item Drop Rate (Unique or Legendary) - the doc calls it useful on both server types, for farming and for boss drops

Attack (Unique) - the former recommendation, now demoted; the doc's reasoning is that with the release of HEXA skills it is more beneficial to gain buff duration uptime for use during the Origin skill. Still acceptable as a stopgap while Honor EXP is low
rejected: Attack Speed - 'We can self-cap on attack speed with a green pot only.'
Critical Rate - okay to keep in the early game to help proc the Hayato link, otherwise not that useful
% Skip Chance - 'This does not skip any important skill so unfortunately it is not usable.'
Passive Skills Level +1 - the doc says this has been calculated and is weaker than the ideal set
innerAbility.sourceCountNote: Grandis lists the same three ideal lines (Boss Damage +20%, Buff Duration +38%, Damage to monsters inflicted with Abnormal Status +8%, re-read 2026-09-12) but credits 'Class Doc' for its Inner Ability field - one lineage. Downgraded from 'moderate' on 2026-09-12. Alternatives and rejections are class doc only.
innerAbility.notes: Buff Duration being a first-class Buccaneer inner ability line is a 6th-job-era change, tied to keeping buffs up through the Origin skill window. On Reboot/Heroic specifically the doc prefers Meso Obtained during the progression phase over the ideal damage set.

gearingNotes: CRITICAL RATE: Buccaneer exceeds the critical rate cap against bosses from its own passives with no outside help, so bossing hyper stat points should not go into Critical Rate. The class does still want 100% visual critical rate, purely to trigger Hayato's Moonlight Blade Learnings link skill. The doc enumerates the cheap sources as Legion Familiar badges 3%, base 5%, Legion members Night Lord and Marksman 8-10%, Decent Sharp Eyes 10%, Precision Strikes 15%, Shadow Heart 20%, Legion Artifact 20% - totalling 81-83% - and fills the gap with the Lynn link (10% crit plus 10% damage), Legion grid blocks, and as little hyper stat as possible because the higher crit hyper stat levels return poorly. ATTACK SPEED: the knuckle chain is attack speed 5 base, 7 with Speed Infusion, 9 with Knuckle Mastery, and exactly 10 with a green potion - so a green potion is required, and the +attack speed inner ability line is redundant. IED TARGETS: Lotus through Verus Hilla, 85% minimum and 93% ideal; Black Mage through lower-difficulty Grandis bosses, 95% minimum; hard bosses, 97% or better. WSE POTENTIAL: between 9/0/0 and 7/2/0 attack/boss/IED lines is considered the ideal band, and the doc advises dropping IED lines off WSE later since set effects and other sources cover it. COOLDOWN HAT: the doc calls Buccaneer the worst class in the game for a cooldown hat and says a stat hat wins by a wide margin; the only exception is a -2 CD hat in min-cut scenarios where it buys one extra burst. RINGS: as of the Frieren collaboration patch Continuous and Ring of Restraint can be worn together; Ring of Restraint gets upgrade priority in both cases - to level 5 so it matches the length of the Origin skill, and to level 6 for the large attack-percentage jump between 5 and 6. All of the above is from The Buccaneer Bible (2026-09-10) unless otherwise noted, and is single-source. SCOPE NOTE: this field sits outside the five endgame sections this resolution pass was scoped to, and was NOT re-verified line by line on 2026-09-12.

commonMistakes.mistake: Activating or double-clicking the Pirate Blessing link skill.
commonMistakes.why: While the buff is active it swaps the STR and DEX values on your gear, which costs a large amount of damage. You can tell it happened by checking the buff bar.
The class doc rates Buccaneer as the worst class for cooldown hats; a stat hat is better by a large margin outside of -2 CD min-cut edge cases.

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting bossing hyper stat points into Critical Rate.
commonMistakes.why: The class doc states Buccaneer 'already has over 100% critical rate when attacking bosses', and that higher crit hyper stat levels have bad returns.
The green potion is the last step that takes knuckle attack speed from 9 to 10; without it the class is permanently a stage short.

commonMistakes.mistake: Stopping a Sol Janus investment partway between breakpoints.
commonMistakes.why: Major upgrades land at Sol Janus levels 10, 20 and 30; intermediate levels only add damage and EXP, so a half-finished push is wasted resource. maplestorywiki's Sol Janus level table shows the matching EXP steps (Lv. 9 26% to Lv. 10 37%, Lv. 19 55% to Lv. 20 67%, Lv. 29 85% to Lv. 30 100%).

commonMistakes.mistake: Standing still for long stretches while Lord of the Deep is up.
commonMistakes.why: The class doc states the toggle 'Will stop registering hits if you stand still for too long (approximately 25 seconds)'.

commonMistakes.mistake: Skipping the Nautilus Strike boost because the skill is not in the rotation.
commonMistakes.why: The boost is taken for the passive, not for casting the skill: Nautilus Strike grants 2 additional final-attack hits when you attack with Somersault Kick, Corkscrew Blow, Octopunch, Serpent Vortex, Howling Fist, or the initial cast of Unleash Neptunus. It does NOT trigger on the Neptunus Enrage portals that follow. maplestorywiki carries the full in-game list; the class doc states the same list but omits Somersault Kick. The doc also notes the skill does not need to be off cooldown for the passive to apply.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on Buccaneer's iframes to survive.
commonMistakes.why: The iframes are tied to the burst - one second per Lightning Form orb, up to three, plus a few seconds after Howling Fist's mouth closes - and the class doc advises against treating them as a survival tool.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm. A resolution pass on 2026-09-12 then re-opened each cited page and settled every defect touching the five endgame sections.

resolved.defect: FABRICATED SOURCE ATTRIBUTION - vMatrix.priority[Hook Bomber].consensus claimed 'Grandis separately ranks the Hook Bomber node SECONDARY'.
resolved.resolution: The defect was right that the file was wrong, and wrong about what the truth is. Re-read grandislibrary.com/explorers/buccaneer on 2026-09-12 including the page's embedded node data: 'primary':[0,1,2,3] and 'other':[4,5], with the rendered Node 1-4 chips in the primary colour (#2E94B6) and Node 5-6 in grey (#6C757D). So Grandis places Hook Bomber (Node 4) in PRIMARY, not SECONDARY - and contrary to the defect's own 'verbatim' quote, Grandis assigns NO Buccaneer node to SECONDARY (the SECONDARY legend is a static tier definition shown on every class page). The false attribution has been removed from the entry. The defect was also right that a real conflict was being buried: the class doc puts Hook Bomber in Lower Priority while Grandis puts its node alongside Octopunch. That is now a first-class entry in conflicts[], with each side's stated criterion.

resolved.defect: FABRICATED GLOSS - 'the opening cast of Unleash Neptunus', a list that drops Somersault Kick and drops the Neptunus Enrage exclusion, appearing in vMatrix.priority[Raging Serpent Assault + Nautilus Strike].why and commonMistakes[6].why.
resolved.resolution: Partly refuted, partly upheld. REFUTED: the phrase is not a fabrication. The Buccaneer Bible says verbatim '2 additional hits for 165% Damage when attacking with Corkscrew Blow, Octopunch, Serpent Vortex, Howling Fist, and the initial cast of Unleash Neptunus (but not the Neptunus Enrage portals afterwards)', and again in its FAQ 'the initial cast of Unleash Neptunus'. 'Opening cast' was a faithful paraphrase of 'initial cast', not an invention. The defect's premise that the game 'names a distinct skill, Release Neptunus' is also unsafe: maplestorywiki's 4th-job Nautilus Strike tooltip says Release Neptunus while its HEXA Nautilus Strike tooltip says Unleash Neptunus, and Unleash Neptunus is the name of the actual Origin skill on that same page - one skill, two tooltip translations. UPHELD: the file's list did drop Somersault Kick (present in the wiki's game text, absent from the class doc) and did drop the Neptunus Enrage exclusion (present in BOTH sources). Both occurrences rewritten to the full wiki list including Somersault Kick and the exclusion, with maplestorywiki added alongside the class doc and the tooltip naming discrepancy recorded.

resolved.defect: FABRICATED ORDERING - hexa.order step 1's masteries-before-Sol-Janus sequence. 'No source states it; the file's own conflicts[2] declares that no textual HEXA levelling order was obtainable.'
resolved.resolution: The claim is stated outright in the cited source. Verbatim from the Buccaneer Bible's Sol Janus section, re-read as raw text 2026-09-12: 'You should unlock Sol Janus right after you unlocked some of the masteries as this skill helps a lot with both farming and just doing dailies/weeklies.' The defect's supporting argument rested on a real ambiguity in the file's own wording, so that has been fixed too: conflicts[hexa] and the new hexa.knownGap now state explicitly that the missing item is the per-node priority CHART (an embedded image), not HEXA sequencing advice in general, so the two can no longer be confused. Step 1 retained and quoted; sourceCount 1, consensus weak.

alsoChangedThisPass: Re-labelled every endgame claim with sources / sourceCount / consensus / verifiedAt under the independent-lineage rule.

DOWNGRADED hyperSkills from 'moderate' to weak and innerAbility from 'moderate' to weak. Grandis's Credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc', so those agreements are one lineage, not two votes. The old labels overstated support.
DOWNGRADED vMatrix.priority[Static Thumper] from 'moderate' to weak for the same lineage reason.
DOWNGRADED vMatrix.trios[boost node groups] from 'strong' to moderate: confirmed on exactly two independent pages, and strong requires 3+.

RESOLVED the 'contested / possibly stale' flag on both trios and REMOVED the trio conflict entry. Grandis's current v.269 page lists a Primary Trio (Octopunch, Sea Serpent's Rage/Raging Serpent Assault, Nautilus Strike) and a Secondary Trio (Hook Bomber, Sea Serpent Burst/Serpent Assault, Corkscrew Blow) matching mystyjl's 2024 data exactly, so the staleness worry is not borne out. The supposed redundancy problem dissolves as well: Grandis's own note says a trio is composed of each node's MAIN skill and that 'Nodes with the same Main Skill (skill at the top) cannot be equipped at the same time', so three different main skills drawn from one enhancement group is legal.
DELETED the unsourced '(top line)' annotation on the +20% Boss Damage inner ability line.

SHAPE FIX: innerAbility.ideal and the hyperSkills passive lists are now explicitly flagged unordered (idealIsOrdered / passivesAreOrdered false) because no source ranks their members. Conversely hyperStats.priority, vMatrix.priority and hexa.order now carry orderIsStated true with a note naming the evidence - the class doc writes the hyper stat priorities literally with arrows, and tiers its V Matrix list - so array position is warranted rather than invented.

CORRECTED conflicts[linkSkill.levels]: the file said Grandis stated 100 all stat; Grandis's skill data says +130, agreeing with maplestorywiki. Left as an open conflict because linkSkill is outside this pass's endgame scope, but the misattribution is fixed.
Left untouched by instruction: gearingNotes (now carrying a scope note saying it was not re-verified this pass) and all other non-endgame content.

writtenNote: The five endgame sections (vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility) now contain only claims re-opened and re-verified against their cited pages on 2026-09-12, each labelled with an independent source count. hexa carries one documented ABSENCE - the per-node HEXA levelling chart, published in the class doc as an image - recorded as hexa.knownGap rather than guessed at. A disclosed gap is not an unverified claim, so this flag is set true; the planner must render hexa.knownGap as a gap and must not infer a node order from hexa.order, whose four steps cover Sol Janus and HEXA Stat sequencing only.
